title: CAT 2022 Question Paper (Slot 1, PYQ) - Quantitative Ability - Geometry
subject: Quantitative Ability

questions.q: A trapezium ABCD has side AD parallel to BC, $\angle BAD = 90^\circ$, BC = 3 cm and AD = 8 cm. If the perimeter of this trapezium is 36 cm, then its area, in sq. cm, is
questions.explain: Let AB = $h$ and CD = $x$. Perimeter = $h + x + 3 + 8 = 36 \Rightarrow h + x = 25$. Dropping a perpendicular from C to AD creates a right triangle with legs $h$ and $8-3=5$, and hypotenuse $x$. So $h^2 + 5^2 = x^2 \Rightarrow x^2 - h^2 = 25 \Rightarrow (x-h)(x+h) = 25$. With $x+h=25$, we get $x-h=1$. Solving yields $h = 12$. The area of the trapezium is $\frac{1}{2}(AD+BC) \times h = \frac{1}{2}(8+3) \times 12 = 66$ sq. cm.

questions.q: All the vertices of a rectangle lie on a circle of radius $R$. If the perimeter of the rectangle is $P$, then the area of the rectangle is
questions.explain: Let the length and width of the rectangle be $l$ and $w$. Perimeter $P = 2(l+w) \Rightarrow l+w = P/2$. The diagonal of the rectangle passes through the center of the circle, so $l^2 + w^2 = (2R)^2 = 4R^2$. We want the area $A = lw$. We know $(l+w)^2 = l^2 + w^2 + 2lw$. Substituting our values: $(P/2)^2 = 4R^2 + 2A \Rightarrow P^2/4 = 4R^2 + 2A \Rightarrow 2A = P^2/4 - 4R^2 \Rightarrow A = P^2/8 - 2R^2$.
